'''Eberhard O. Voit''' (born 8 February 1953) is a Clinical Professor at the University of Texas at Dallas. Until 2024, he was a Professor and David D. Flanagan Chair in Biological Systems at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]] and [[Emory University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bme.gatech.edu/bme/faculty/Eberhard-Voit|title=Coulter Department of Biomedical Engineering at Georgia Tech and Emory University|website=bme.gatech.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-11-25}}</ref> and a [[Georgia Research Alliance]] Eminent Scholar.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gra.org/scholar/45/Eberhard_Voit.html|title=Georgia Research Alliance|website=gra.org|language=en|access-date=2018-11-25}}</ref> He is now a Regents' Emeritus Professor.

== Biography ==

Eberhard Otto Voit was born in [[Dortmund]], Germany. He received the Diplom (Master's of Science) in Biology (Zoology, Genetics, Mathematics; 1976), Philosophikum in Philosophy and Education (1977), Staatsexamen (Master's of Science) in Mathematics (1978), and Dr. rer. nat. (Ph.D.) in Developmental and Theoretical Biology (1981) from the [[University of Cologne]]. From 1981 to 1982, he was a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Microbiology and Immunology at the [[University of Michigan]], Ann Arbor, under the mentorship of Professor [[Michael Antonio Savageau|Michael Savageau]]. He was a member of the Men's Glee Club at the University of Michigan.

Voit held research and faculty positions at the University of Cologne, the University of Michigan, the [[Medical University of South Carolina]] in Charleston, and at the Cooperative Research Centre for Temperate Hardwood Forestry in [[Tasmania, Australia]]. In 2004, he joined the Department of Biomedical Engineering at [[Georgia Tech]] and [[Emory University|Emory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/computational-biology-and-chemistry/editorial-board/eberhard-voit|title=Eberhard Voit|last=|first=|date=|website=www.journals.elsevier.com|publisher=Computational Biology and Chemistry|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-11-25}}</ref> He is now affiliated with the Department of Biological Sciences at the University of Texas at Dallas.

Voit is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/aaas-members-elected-fellows-1|title=AAAS Members Elected as Fellows|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|language=en|access-date=2018-11-25}}</ref> the [[American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering]] (AIMBE)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://aimbe.org/college-of-fellows/cof-1480/|title=Eberhard Voit, Ph.D. COF-1480 - AIMBE|website=aimbe.org|language=en|access-date=2018-11-25}}</ref> and the [[Society for Mathematical Biology]] (SMB).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.smb.org}}</ref> He is furthermore an Overseas Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Medicine]] of the United Kingdom. He was named a notable alumnus of the University of Cologne, as well as a Regents' Emeritus Professor at the Georgia Institute of Technology. 

== Work ==

Voit is recognized as a leading expert in complex biomedical [[systems modeling]] and, in particular, the scientific modeling and systems analysis framework of [[Biochemical Systems Theory]] (BST)<ref>Savageau, M.A. and E.O. Voit: Recasting nonlinear differential equations as S-systems: A canonical nonlinear form. ‘’Mathem. Biosci. ‘’ ‘’’87 ‘’’, 83-115, 1987.</ref><ref>Voit, E.O.: ‘’Computational Analysis of Biochemical Systems. A Practical Guide for Biochemists and Molecular Biologists‘’, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, U.K., 2000.</ref><ref>Voit, E.O.: Biochemical Systems Theory: A review. ‘’Int. Scholarly Res. Network (ISRN – Biomathematics) ‘’, Article 897658, pp. 1-53, 2013.</ref> Voit's team has been developing numerous methodologies within BST and using these, along with other modeling techniques, to analyze biomedical phenomena from microbial dynamics<ref>Dolatshahi, S., L.L. Fonseca, and E.O. Voit: New insights into the complex regulation of the glycolytic pathway in ‘’Lactococcus lactis‘’. ‘’Molecular Biosystems‘’ ‘’’12(1) ‘’’, 23-47, 2016.</ref> and bacterial metapopulations<ref>Dam, P., L.L. Fonseca, K.T. Konstantinidis, and E.O. Voit: Dynamic models of the complex microbial metapopulation of Lake Mendota. ‘’Nature PJ Sys. Biol. Appl. ‘’, ‘’’2 ‘’’, 16007, 2016.</ref> to diseases like schizophrenia<ref>Qi, Z., G. Yu. F. Tretter. O. Pogarell, A.A. Grace and E.O. Voit: A Heuristic Model for Working Memory Deficit in Schizophrenia. ‘’Bioch. Biophys. Acta - Systems Genetics‘’ ‘’’1860 ‘’’, 2696-2705, 2016.</ref> and malaria.<ref>Fonseca, L.L., H.A. Alezi, A. Moreno, J.W. Barnwell, M.R. Galinski, and E.O. Voit: Quantifying the removal of red blood cells in ‘’Macaca mulatta‘’ during a ‘’Plasmodium coatneyi‘’ infection. ‘’Malaria J. ‘’ ‘’’15 ‘’’, 410, 2016.</ref> He has also worked in the areas of computational statistics<ref>Rust, P.F. and E.O. Voit: Statistical densities, cumulatives, quantiles, and power obtained by S-system differential equations. ‘’ J. Americ. Stat. Assoc. (JASA)‘’ ‘’’85 (410) ‘’’, 572-578, 1990.</ref><ref>Voit, E.O.: The S-distribution. A tool for approximation and classification of univariate, unimodal probability distributions. ‘’Biometrical J. ‘’ ‘’’34 (7) ‘’’, 855-878, 1992.</ref> and [[metabolic engineering]].<ref>Voit, E.O.: Optimization in integrated biochemical systems. ‘’Biotechn. Bioengin. ‘’ ‘’’40 ‘’’, 572-582, 1992.</ref><ref>Torres, N.V., and E.O. Voit: ‘’Pathway Analysis and Optimization in Metabolic Engineering‘’. Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, U.K., 2002.</ref>

Voit has documented these advancements in about 300 [[scientific journal]] articles and book chapters. He is also the author of several books, some with translations into Chinese and Korean,<ref>Voit, E.O.: ‘’A First Course in Systems Biology‘’. Garland Science, New York, NY, 2012; second edition 2016., including ''A First Course in Systems Biology''</ref> an introductory text for undergraduate and graduate students, and ''The Inner Workings of Life: Vignettes in Systems Biology''<ref>Voit, E.O.: ‘’The Inner Workings of Life. Vignettes in Systems Biology‘’, Cambridge University Press, Cambridge, U.K., 2016.</ref> a non-technical introduction to [[systems biology]] for educated non-experts.
